strengths: The focus on rendering memory rather than compressed file size addresses an important practical limitation of 3D Gaussian Splatting.

Table 1 reports substantial improvements across three standard datasets. On Mip-NeRF360, static/rendering memory decreases from GaussianSpa’s 115/448 MB to 55/265 MB, with nearly identical PSNR and improved LPIPS.

Arbitrarily oriented spherical Gaussian lobes provide a plausible compact color representation. The color-representation comparisons and pruning ablations support the usefulness of the design, and the analytic color compensation has a sound mathematical motivation.
weaknesses: The central claim of jointly optimizing a total memory budget is not adequately supported by the implemented algorithm. Equations 11–12 replace the coupled projection with separate primitive and lobe budgets, without specifying how these budgets are allocated or updated under the total constraint. This demonstrates simultaneous sparsification, but does not establish the claimed optimization of the trade-off between primitive count and per-primitive complexity.

The optimization description contains material inconsistencies. Algorithm 1 omits the rho weights present in the quadratic penalties of Equation 7, and selection using arbitrary importance metrics is not generally the proximal operator of Equation 8. Calling the method ADMM-inspired is reasonable, but the relationship between the stated objective and the implemented heuristic needs clarification.

The memory constraint is insufficiently justified. Equation 6 counts nonzero lobes even when their parent primitive has zero opacity, although those lobes need not be stored. The base cost of 11 parameters and the stated dimension of Theta are also not reconciled with the geometry, diffuse color, and lobe attributes. Consequently, the connection between the constraint and actual memory consumption is unclear.

The memory evaluation has consequential limitations. Some baseline memory figures are estimated from primitive counts rather than measured, although dynamic memory also depends on projected footprints and renderer behavior. The PyTorch measurement procedure lacks precise counter and peak-reset details, and averaging per-view peaks does not establish the worst-case memory required to run a scene on a constrained device.

Reproducibility and comparison at controlled budgets are incomplete. The manuscript does not specify the allocation of primitive/lobe budgets, pruning thresholds, penalty settings, SG initialization, or scene-dependent operator choices. The two proposed operating points are unlabeled, and no quality–memory curves establish robustness across budgets. The ablations use different achieved memory footprints and leave baseline tuning insufficiently documented.

Novelty and deployment claims exceed the evidence. SG-Splatting already uses spherical Gaussians, and GaussianSpa supplies the underlying sparsification framework; the contribution is therefore a specific extension and integration rather than a fundamentally new representation or paradigm. Figure 1 provides an encouraging mobile demonstration, but lacks a systematic protocol covering resolution, memory, quality, and competing compressed methods.

strengths: The paper addresses a practically important distinction between storage compression and rendering-memory reduction, explicitly measuring both static and rendering VRAM.

The reported results are promising across three standard datasets. On Mip-NeRF360, MEGS2 reduces static/rendering VRAM from GaussianSpa’s 115/448 MB to 55/265 MB, with nearly unchanged PSNR and improved LPIPS.
Figure 3 provides useful evidence that arbitrarily oriented spherical Gaussian lobes offer a better quality–parameter trade-off than the tested spherical-harmonic and orthogonal-axis alternatives.
The color-compensation formula is well motivated, and Table 4 includes relevant ablations of soft pruning, simultaneous pruning, and compensation.
weaknesses: The central claim of unified memory-budget optimization is not adequately supported by the implemented algorithm. Equations 11–12 replace the coupled constraint with separate primitive and lobe quotas, without explaining how these quotas are selected or adjusted to allocate a common budget. Independent projections with prescribed quotas generally do not solve Equation 8. Moreover, arbitrary importance rankings are not necessarily proximal operators for its stated quadratic objective. The method may be a useful simultaneous pruning heuristic, but the claimed optimal allocation between primitive count and lobe complexity is unsubstantiated.

The mathematical specification contains consequential inconsistencies. Equation 6 assigns 11 base parameters per primitive, whereas the described position, rotation, scale, opacity, and diffuse RGB require 14. The stated dimension of Θ omits the additional lobe directions and amplitudes. The budget also counts lobes independently of whether their parent primitive survives. Finally, Algorithm 1 omits the distinct penalty weights appearing in Equation 7. These discrepancies undermine the interpretation of the objective as an accurate parameter budget and leave the implemented optimization unclear.

Reproducibility is insufficient for the main contribution. The manuscript does not specify the actual budgets, their decomposition into primitive/lobe quotas, penalty settings, pruning thresholds, SG initialization, or selection between the proposed sharpness and range criteria. It also does not explain how variable-length lobe data are packed and accessed during rendering, although that implementation is essential to realizing the reported memory savings.

The evaluation does not sufficiently establish the quality–memory frontier. Most baselines have only one operating point, and the pruning ablations use different achieved memory footprints without reporting matched budgets, tuning procedures, or training allocations. The unusually poor GaussianSpa-plus-Reduced3DGS result needs further implementation detail and controlled comparison. These experiments support the complete pipeline but do not cleanly establish the claimed superiority of joint budget allocation.

Memory and deployment evidence has important limitations. LP-3DGS and Mini-Splatting memory numbers are estimated rather than measured, despite rendering memory depending on visibility and projected footprint as well as primitive count. PyTorch memory measurements exclude some device overhead, and averaging per-view peaks does not establish worst-case device requirements. Figure 1 reports mobile frame rates without a reproducible protocol covering resolution, viewer configuration, memory consumption, or baseline failure conditions.

Novelty and scope are overstated. SG-based appearance and ADMM-inspired primitive pruning already appear in the cited SG-Splatting and GaussianSpa work; the contribution is principally their extension through free lobe orientations and simultaneous lobe sparsification. Claims of pioneering SG appearance, globally optimal memory use, and fundamentally solving the rendering-memory bottleneck exceed the evidence, particularly because dynamic rendering memory is explicitly excluded from the optimization.

strengths: Addresses an important deployment problem: rendering memory rather than compressed file size. Distinguishing static storage in VRAM from rendering-time allocations is practically useful.

Reports substantial gains across three standard datasets. On Mip-NeRF360, memory decreases from GaussianSpa’s 115/448 MB static/rendering footprint to 55/265 MB, with nearly identical PSNR and improved LPIPS.

Includes relevant comparisons and component ablations. Figure 3 supports the parameter efficiency of freely oriented spherical Gaussians, and Table 4 provides evidence for soft pruning, simultaneous optimization, and color compensation.
The color compensation formula has a clear mathematical motivation: replacing a removed lobe with its spherical mean minimizes the stated integrated squared error.
weaknesses: The central unified-budget optimization claim is insufficiently supported. Equations 11–12 replace the coupled projection with separate primitive and lobe quotas, without explaining how these quotas are derived from the total budget or adaptively exchange capacity. Arbitrary importance rankings also do not generally solve the proximal problem in Equation 8. The implementation therefore supports simultaneous pruning, but does not establish the claimed optimal allocation under a unified memory constraint.

The mathematical specification contains consequential inconsistencies. Equation 6 assigns 11 parameters per primitive, apparently omitting the three diffuse-color parameters required in addition to position, rotation, scale, and opacity. It also counts sharpness entries independently of whether their parent primitive survives. Algorithm 1 omits the distinct penalty weights present in Equation 7. These issues require clarification before the memory objective and its implementation can be assessed reliably.

Reproducibility is insufficient for the main contribution. The paper does not specify the actual budgets, quota-selection procedure, penalty settings, pruning thresholds, scene-dependent operator choices, or packing scheme for variable lobe counts. The two proposed configurations in Table 1 are not identified by their settings. Referring to GaussianSpa’s training procedure does not resolve these new implementation choices.

The evaluation does not adequately establish a controlled memory–quality frontier. Most baselines have a single operating point, and the sequential and hard-pruning ablations use different achieved memory footprints without documenting matched tuning or training budgets. Some baseline memory results are estimated from primitive counts even though dynamic memory also depends on projected geometry and tile overlap. Per-scene results and variability are absent.

The edge-device claims exceed the supporting measurements. Figure 1 reports selected WebGL frame rates, but provides no systematic mobile memory measurements, resolution and rendering settings, or comparisons with compressed baselines. Averaging per-view peak PyTorch allocations also does not establish the worst-case device memory requirement.

Novelty is narrower than the paper’s framing suggests: spherical-Gaussian color modeling already appears in SG-Splatting, and the sparsification framework builds directly on GaussianSpa. The useful combination and free lobe orientations could constitute a contribution, but the unresolved optimization and evaluation issues currently prevent a convincing acceptance case.
